samples.summary: Thirty-day sweep is cross-account but its open-document guard is scoped to one account, so it can purge another account's live entry in another tab
samples.evidence: `OfflineRuntime` builds the housekeeping store with `isOpenElsewhere: (docKey) => isOpenInAnyTab(docKey, { userId, whenUnknown: false })` (packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx:75-81). `isOpenInAnyTab` narrows the lock-name prefix to `wb-durable:{thisUserId}:` (packages/frontend/src/lib/durable-session.ts, `prefix` computation in `isOpenInAnyTab`). But `WafflebaseDocStore.collectStale` deliberately enumerates aged headers for EVERY account on the device (`const aged = await this.headerKeysWhere(BY_UPDATED_AT, range)` — unscoped, and the doc-comment says "Live entries are collected **whoever wrote them**"). The two do not line up: a document held open by a DIFFERENT account in another tab holds `wb-durable:{otherUserId}:{docKey}`, which the user-scoped prefix filter never matches, so `isLive()` answers false and the entry is purged out from under that tab's live client. The `evicted` marker that would make the next append fail loudly is keyed per database in this tab's module memory (`evictedKeys` in wafflebase-doc-store.ts), so the other tab never sees it and its appends fall into the contract's silent "no base" success while its chip still reports the document saved. Reachability is limited by `load()` touching `updatedAt` on attach, so it needs a tab open longer than the max age — but the guard/scope mismatch is real and the fix belongs either on the sweep (scope it, or ask unscoped) or on `openElsewhere` (drop `userId` for the collector).

samples.summary: The chip's "turn on offline saving" offer is reachable on the share-link route, where NonDurableScope guarantees it can never apply and the visitor may have no account
samples.evidence: `SharedHeaderStatus` renders `<SyncStatusChip />` for every editor-role share-link visitor (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-header-status.tsx:26), and that subtree is inside the new `NonDurableScope` added at packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:1014. The chip's new offer is gated only on `stranded && supportsClientKey() && !offlineEnabled` — it never consults `useDurabilityPermitted()` or the `not-permitted` lapse it already reads via `useDurabilityLapse()`. So a stranded share-link visitor gets a clickable chip and a toast action offering to "Turn on for later documents", a per-device preference that can never apply to anything reached through a share link, and that for an anonymous visitor (no `userId` ⇒ `useDurableDocument` always refuses) can never apply to anything at all. The chip still works; it is the offer that is out of step with the guard this change introduced. Fix belongs on the new code: fold `permitted` (or `lapse === 'not-permitted'`) into `offerOffline` in sync-status-chip.tsx.

samples.summary: OfflineRuntime runs unconditionally for every authenticated session — creating the IndexedDB database and issuing an extra full GET /documents — even though the pinned SDK makes the feature inert
samples.evidence: `<OfflineRuntime userId={String(me.id)} />` is mounted for every signed-in user at packages/frontend/src/PrivateRoute.tsx:35, and its effect (packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx:63-160) has no `supportsClientKey()` and no `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled()` gate. Every authenticated session therefore opens/creates the `wafflebase-offline` IndexedDB database via `store.collectStale()` (offline-runtime.tsx:111) and issues an additional uncached `fetchDocuments()` (offline-runtime.tsx, `const accessible = await fetchDocuments()`) to the backend's unpaginated `GET /documents`, which lists every document across every workspace the user belongs to (packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:181-195). With `@yorkie-js/react` pinned to `0.7.22` (packages/frontend/package.json:66) and `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` (packages/frontend/src/lib/yorkie-capabilities.ts), `supportsClientKey()` is false, so nothing is ever written to that store — the cost lands on all users and on the documents endpoint for a feature that is dark. Nothing breaks; it is a per-session cost the rest of the app did not previously pay.

samples.summary: deleteWorkspace now makes two extra network round-trips before the DELETE, changing the cost and request shape seen by its only UI caller
samples.evidence: `deleteWorkspaceMutation` calls `deleteWorkspace(workspaceId!)` at packages/frontend/src/app/workspaces/workspace-settings.tsx:182. That function now runs `documentIdsIn(id)` first (packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:127 → :101-115), which issues a `fetchWorkspace(ref)` plus a full account-wide `fetchDocuments()` — the unpaginated list of every document in every workspace the user belongs to — before the DELETE is even attempted. The same two calls run on `removeMember` whenever the member being removed is the signed-in user (workspaces.ts:159-160). The caller still works (failures are swallowed by `documentIdsIn`'s catch), but the operation is now three sequential round-trips where it was one, and `api/workspaces.ts` now depends on `api/documents.ts` (workspaces.ts:5), a new edge between two API modules. The pre-existing `url.test.ts` per-request assertion had to be weakened to tolerate the extra request that carries no id (packages/frontend/src/api/url.test.ts:156-175), which is the visible symptom of the same change.

samples.summary: deleteDocuments' new comment describes a partial-success contract the backend does not have
samples.evidence: The added comment at packages/frontend/src/api/documents.ts:211-213 and the matching test at packages/frontend/src/api/documents.test.ts:152-159 assert that "the route is manager-gated per id, so a partial answer is ordinary". The producer disagrees: `POST /documents/delete` collects `denied` ids and throws `ForbiddenException` if ANY of them fail the manager check, then returns `{ deleted: body.ids }` verbatim (packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:400-437). The endpoint is all-or-nothing, so `result.deleted` is always the full input or the call throws. The defensive `result.deleted ?? []` is harmless and the runtime behaviour is correct; the comment and the test's stated rationale describe a contract that does not exist, which is the sort of thing the next person changing this route will trust.

finding.summary: Thirty-day sweep is cross-account but its open-document guard is scoped to one account, so it can purge another account's live entry in another tab
finding.evidence: `OfflineRuntime` builds the housekeeping store with `isOpenElsewhere: (docKey) => isOpenInAnyTab(docKey, { userId, whenUnknown: false })` (packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx:75-81). `isOpenInAnyTab` narrows the lock-name prefix to `wb-durable:{thisUserId}:` (packages/frontend/src/lib/durable-session.ts, `prefix` computation in `isOpenInAnyTab`). But `WafflebaseDocStore.collectStale` deliberately enumerates aged headers for EVERY account on the device (`const aged = await this.headerKeysWhere(BY_UPDATED_AT, range)` — unscoped, and the doc-comment says "Live entries are collected **whoever wrote them**"). The two do not line up: a document held open by a DIFFERENT account in another tab holds `wb-durable:{otherUserId}:{docKey}`, which the user-scoped prefix filter never matches, so `isLive()` answers false and the entry is purged out from under that tab's live client. The `evicted` marker that would make the next append fail loudly is keyed per database in this tab's module memory (`evictedKeys` in wafflebase-doc-store.ts), so the other tab never sees it and its appends fall into the contract's silent "no base" success while its chip still reports the document saved. Reachability is limited by `load()` touching `updatedAt` on attach, so it needs a tab open longer than the max age — but the guard/scope mismatch is real and the fix belongs either on the sweep (scope it, or ask unscoped) or on `openElsewhere` (drop `userId` for the collector).

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out in the repository. offline-runtime.tsx:75-81 supplies the store's open-document guard as `isOpenInAnyTab(docKey, { userId, whenUnknown: false })`, and durable-session.ts:329-338 narrows the lock match to the prefix `wb-durable:{thisUserId}:` — a lock minted by durableLockName (durable-session.ts:69-71) for a different account can never match. Meanwhile WafflebaseDocStore.collectStale reads aged headers unscoped (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1167 via headerKeysWhere at 1285-1295: a plain BY_UPDATED_AT range over the whole HEADERS store, with no BY_USER intersection and no belongsToAnotherUser filter — that filter is used only by orphanSnapshotKeys at 1253), and its own comment at 1144-1151 states cross-account collection is deliberate while 1164-1166 asserts the live-document exemption as an invariant. isLive (397-402) delegates that exemption entirely to the user-scoped callback, so another account's open document is seen as idle and purged at 1174-1185. The compensating `evicted` marker is tab-local module memory keyed by db name (189-198), and the file itself concedes at 184-187 that another tab's client is left unmarked, so the victim tab gets the silent 'no base' success the sweep's comment at 1176-1184 warns about. Reachability is narrowed by load() calling touch() (532-537, 555-572) but not closed: the repo's own test at wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts:512-524 treats an attached-but-untouched document over two months as plausible, and it is protected only by the same-instance `touched` set; the cross-tab test at 563-580 pins the exemption only for a matching userId, leaving the cross-account case uncovered. No guard, caller, or filter elsewhere makes this unreachable, so none of not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope applies — this is a guard-scope mismatch reached from a path outside the guard, squarely in the blast-radius lane.

finding.summary: Swallowing a failed `local-changes-dropped` subscription silently breaks the `expectLoss`-before-`remove` invariant the store relies on, turning an archive into an outright delete of unsent work
finding.evidence: `DurableLossWatch` is the ONLY production caller of `expectLoss` (`packages/frontend/src/components/durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:282`; grep for `expectLoss` finds no other non-test call site). `WafflebaseDocStore.remove()` reads that latch at `packages/frontend/src/lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts:771` and only writes an archive when it is set (`if (record && losing)` at line 791), documented at lines 735-737 as "The latch is set from the `LocalChangesDropped` handler ... so the flag is always in place by the time the removal arrives." This delta wraps the subscription in `try { ... } catch { console.warn(...) }` for exactly the case the new comment cites — an SDK where `subscribe('local-changes-dropped')` throws `Unsupported event type`. On such an SDK the handler is never registered, yet the SDK still calls `store.remove()` on its three loss paths, so the removal takes the `losing === false` branch: snapshot, header and change log are deleted with no archive, `listRecoverableWork` has nothing to list, and the user's unreconciled edits are gone with only a console warning. Before this change the throw was loud (it crashed the subtree, so the document was not editable and nothing was silently deleted); after it, editing continues over a store whose loss path now deletes. Fix belongs on the new code: when the loss subscription specifically cannot be installed, the durable store must not be handed to the client as an archiving store (e.g. disable persistence / report undurable) rather than just warning. Confidence is medium only because node_modules is not installed here, so I could not confirm whether @yorkie-js/sdk 0.7.22 emits this event — but the diff's own justification asserts it may not.

verdict.reason: All three load-bearing claims check out in the tree. (1) The swallow exists: durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:268-278 wraps subscriptions in try/catch with only a console.warn, and the `local-changes-dropped` subscription that calls `durable.store.expectLoss(doc.getKey())` (line 281-282) runs through it; no durability state is latched off on failure (value.durable at line 181 stays true). (2) That is the sole production caller of `expectLoss` — a repo-wide grep returns only durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:282 plus test files. (3) The consumer outside the diff relies on the latch: wafflebase-doc-store.ts:771 reads `expectedLosses`, line 791 `if (record && losing)` is the only writer of an ArchiveRecord, and lines 809-811 delete snapshot/header/changes unconditionally — so an unregistered handler turns the SDK's loss-path `remove()` into an outright delete of unsent work, contradicting the stated invariant at wafflebase-doc-store.ts:735-737. Possible refutations fail: the feature is version-gated by supportsClientKey() (yorkie-capabilities.ts:76-82, MinClientKeyVersion 0.7.23 vs current 0.7.22 pin), but that gates whether the store is mounted, not whether the latch is installed — once bumped, the store is live to the SDK whether or not the subscribe call was accepted. I could not prove the throw branch unreachable: node_modules is absent, @yorkie-js/sdk is not vendored, and docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:534 still lists PersistDisabled as upstream SDK work, so the event-name strings are unverified. The finding is also in-lane for blast radius — the damage site (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:791) is outside the diff and is an invariant another module assumes.

finding.summary: A swallowed `persist-disabled` subscription leaves the durability chip reporting "Saved to this device" for a document the SDK has stopped persisting
finding.evidence: `reportPersistDisabled()` is the only thing that latches durability off for the SDK-gave-up case; consumers read it via `useDocumentDurability()` (`packages/frontend/src/lib/durable-document-context.ts`, rendered by the sync-status chip — see `packages/frontend/tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:659` and `packages/frontend/src/components/sync-status/sync-status-tooltip.ts:34`). With the new `watch()` helper a `subscribe('persist-disabled')` that throws is reduced to a `console.warn`, so the chip keeps asserting the document is saved locally while it is not — the opposite of the in-diff comment's claim that "an SDK that cannot report a lapse costs the chip its certainty". The certainty is exactly what is kept. The default when the event cannot be watched should be "not durable", not "durable".

verdict.reason: The code is present as described — `watch()` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:269-278) swallows a throwing `doc.subscribe('persist-disabled', …)` (line 292-296) into a `console.warn`, and `durable` defaults true (line 181). But the finding names no site outside the diff that is broken or bypassing. There is exactly one producer of the durability context (`DurableDocumentScope` at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:219; grep for `DurableDocumentScope|durable:` across packages/frontend/src finds no other), so no alternate entry point reaches the "saved" state around the new latch. The cited consumers are unaffected by any contract change: `use-sync-status.ts:75` and `durable-document-context.ts:74-76` consume a boolean whose type and default (`?? false`) are unchanged, and `sync-status-tooltip.ts:1` imports only the `DurabilityLapse` type. The one contract that did change — `DurableDocumentValue.reportPersistDisabled` (durable-document-context.ts:39) — has every construction site updated (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:183; sync-status-chip.test.tsx:110; use-sync-status.test.ts:421,451). The whole argument (swallowed error -> latch never set -> default stays `durable`) is statable from the changed file alone, fifteen lines apart, which the rubric explicitly assigns to the correctness/design-fit lenses ("Logic inside the diff"; "A finding you can state without leaving the diff belongs to another lens"). Real or not, it is not a blast-radius defect: no guard bypass, no unupdated caller, no invariant violated at an untouched site.
